name: Termi Protocol
description: A 3D simulation environment that visualizes AI coding agent workflows in real-time. Instead of watching scrolling terminal output, developers can see their AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, etc.) working as robots in an immersive 3D workspace with desks, file locks, and collaboration features. The tool provides multi-agent sync mode, checkpoints for time-travel debugging, on-device memory, and one-tap approval for risky actions.
community_quotes: The watch-it-work idea is strongest when the room has a hard mapping to operational state, not just animation.
Giving CLI agents a literal body in a 3D room is a clever way to make what Claude Code / Codex are actually doing legible instead of scrolling terminal logs.
The local-first angle is the part I'd trust most here. For AI coding agents, visibility is useful only if it helps me make a decision: pause, approve, rewind, or compare what two agents changed.
You can already do this inside the Command Center through the History section. From there, you can review what the agent did, see recent activity, inspect tool calls.
The visualization also runs fully local. Your file activity, command activity, and agent workflow are not sent to a hosted backend for rendering.
